answer: An agent economy can make each identity post a refundable bond before it may trade, then slash that bond when a dispute proves deliberate fraud. The bond is tied to an auditable payment credential, not merely a fresh account name, so creating a thousand aliases does not create free influence: each must lock real capital. Honest agents recover the stake, while a sybil operator pays the opportunity cost of tying up funds and risks losing them. Like pigment tracked across a meadow island, the bond trail makes clustered identities costly to wash away.
